name: LT1054CN8#PBF
title: LT1054/LT1054L switched-capacitor voltage converter with regulator
summary: A bipolar switched-capacitor converter that inverts or doubles a supply with no inductor, and has its own 2.5 V reference and error amplifier so an external divider makes the output regulated. The LT1054 runs from 3.5 V to 15 V and delivers 100 mA with about 1.1 V lost; the LT1054L runs from 3.5 V to 7 V and delivers 125 mA. FB/SHDN doubles as a shutdown input, OSC retunes or synchronises the 25 kHz oscillator, and parts can be paralleled. It is pin compatible with the LTC1044 and ICL7660 and comes in 8-pin DIP, 8-pin SO and 16-pin wide SO.

notes: LT1054 parts take 3.5 V to 15 V and deliver 100 mA; the LT1054L (LT1054LCS8) takes 3.5 V to 7 V and delivers 125 mA.
C is the 0°C to 100°C grade, I the –40°C to 100°C grade, M the –55°C to 125°C grade. The grade is shown on a label on the shipping container.
Some packages come on 500-unit reels with the #TRMPBF suffix through designated sales channels.

pins.name: FB/SHDN
pins.function: Feedback and shutdown. It is the inverting input of the error amplifier, where a resistor divider sets a regulated output. Pulled under the shutdown threshold (about 0.45 V) it stops the oscillator and the reference/regulator; the switches then let CIN and COUT discharge into the load and supply current falls to about 100 µA. An open-collector gate can drive it.

pins.name: CAP+
pins.function: Positive end of the flying capacitor CIN. It is switched between V+ (sourcing current from V+) and ground (sinking current to ground).

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground.

pins.name: CAP-
pins.function: Negative end of the flying capacitor CIN. It is switched between ground (sinking current to ground) and VOUT (sourcing current from COUT).

pins.name: VOUT
pins.function: Converter output, also connected to the substrate. It must never rise above any other pin: above GND it forward-biases the substrate diode and the part will not start.

pins.name: VREF
pins.function: 2.5 V reference output for regulator dividers, with a positive temperature coefficient that cancels drift in the feedback path. Feedback-network loading is kept to about 60 µA; a short to ground draws about 100 µA without upsetting the regulator, so the pin can serve as the pull-up for OSC.

pins.name: OSC
pins.function: Oscillator timing node, tied inside to Ct ≈ 150 pF that ±7 µA sources charge and discharge for a duty cycle near 50%. A capacitor to ground lowers the frequency, 5 pF to 20 pF from CAP+ raises it, and an external clock can drive it against a pull-up to VREF.

pins.name: V+
pins.function: Supply input. While CIN charges the supply current peaks near 2.2 times the output current; while CIN discharges into COUT it falls to about 0.2 times.

circuits.title: Inverter with start-up transistor for a load referred to the positive supply (Figure 1)
circuits.description: A basic inverter whose load (an op amp is the example) returns to V+ rather than to ground. An NPN switch between the load's negative end and the LT1054 output keeps VOUT from being dragged above GND while the converter starts; RX gives the transistor enough base current to stay saturated at full output current.

parts.note: any small general-purpose NPN; an N-channel enhancement MOSFET may serve in some cases
an op amp drawn as the typical load

notes: IL is the load current, IQ the op amp supply current and IOUT the op amp output current.

circuits.title: Oscillator frequency adjustment and synchronisation (Figure 2)
circuits.description: A basic inverter with the three optional networks on OSC. A capacitor from OSC to ground (C3) slows the oscillator; a 5 pF to 20 pF capacitor from CAP+ to OSC (C4) speeds it up; for synchronisation OSC is pulled up to VREF (a 20k resistor) and an open-collector stage pulls it down at the external clock rate.

parts.note: pull-up from VREF to OSC for synchronisation; optional
open-collector driver for an external clock; optional

notes: Each OSC network is optional and fitted only when wanted; 20k is the recommended pull-up.
OSC is not to be pulled up to an external voltage.

circuits.title: Basic regulator with shutdown and restart inputs (Figure 5)
circuits.description: A positive-to-negative converter whose output is held by the error amplifier: R1 from VREF and R2 from VOUT meet at FB/SHDN, and C1 across R2 keeps light-load regulation good. An NPN on FB/SHDN shuts the part down; a restart pulse or level, divided by R3/R4 and fed through a diode, lifts FB/SHDN so the output can come up without overshoot after a shutdown that left COUT charged.

parts.note: calculated for -5 V with R1 = 20k; the closest 1% value is used
couples the restart signal into FB/SHDN

notes: R3 and R4 are chosen so the restart level at FB/SHDN is 0.7 V to 1.1 V; the restart signal can be a pulse longer than 100 µs or a logic high.
R2/R1 = |VOUT|/(VREF/2 - 40mV) + 1 ≈ |VOUT|/1.21V + 1, VREF = 2.5 V nominal. With R1 = 20k, -5 V gives R2 = 102.6k.

circuits.title: Regulator with a resistor in series with CIN to share the dissipation (Figure 6)
circuits.description: The basic regulator with RX between CAP+ and the flying capacitor. Part of the input-to-output difference is dropped in RX instead of inside the package, which lowers the LT1054's dissipation without changing the regulated output.
notes: In the worked example (12 V to -5 V at 100 mA) RX = 11 Ω takes 490 mW and leaves 450 mW in the LT1054.

circuits.title: Basic voltage inverter
circuits.description: The simplest connection: one flying capacitor between CAP+ and CAP-, an output capacitor on VOUT and a bypass on V+. The output is roughly the negative of the input, less the converter's voltage loss.

circuits.title: Basic voltage inverter/regulator
circuits.description: The inverter with its output regulated: R1 from VREF and R2 from VOUT set the output through FB/SHDN, with 0.002 µF across R2. The flying capacitor is a tenth of the output capacitor.

circuits.title: Negative voltage doubler
circuits.description: Run from a negative input of -3.5 V to -15 V, with V+ at ground and GND at the input. The LT1054 output lies about one input below the input, so the output taken between ground and the collector of QX is about twice the input. QX and RX are a start-up transistor and its base resistor, as in the inverter with start-up transistor.
notes: VIN = -3.5 V to -15 V.
VOUT = 2VIN + (LT1054 voltage loss) + (QX saturation voltage).
The marking on QX and RX points to Figure 3; it should read Figure 1.

circuits.title: Positive doubler
circuits.description: CAP+ swings between V+ and ground and pumps a 10 µF capacitor that hangs from a diode off VIN; a second diode carries the pumped peak to the 100 µF output. GND and VOUT are both grounded and CAP- is left open. Output is about twice the input less the voltage loss and two diode drops, for up to 50 mA.
notes: VIN = 3.5 V to 15 V; VOUT ≈ 2VIN - (VL + 2VDIODE), VL being the LT1054 voltage loss; output 50 mA.

circuits.title: 100mA regulating negative doubler
circuits.description: Two LT1054s, each wired as a negative doubler with two flying capacitors and two 1N4002 diodes, share one output and one feedback node. R1 (from the first part's VREF) and the 500k adjustable R2 set the output; the second part's oscillator is pulled up to its own VREF by 20k and driven through a Schottky from the first part's CAP+. A 1N4002 runs from the output to ground.
notes: VIN = 3.5 V to 15 V; IOUT ≅ 100 mA max.
VOUT max ≈ -2VIN + [LT1054 voltage loss + 2(VDIODE)].

circuits.title: Bipolar supply doubler
circuits.description: One LT1054 makes both a positive and a negative doubled rail. On the positive side a capacitor pumped from CAP+ is charged from VIN through a diode and its peak is passed by a second diode to +VOUT. On the negative side a capacitor pumped from CAP- feeds a diode pair at the LT1054 output and a third diode passes the negative peak to -VOUT. All five diodes are 1N4001.
notes: VIN = 3.5 V to 15 V; +VOUT ≈ 2VIN - (VL + 2VDIODE); -VOUT ≈ -2VIN + (VL + 2VDIODE); VL is the LT1054 voltage loss.

circuits.title: 5V to ±12V converter
circuits.description: From 5 V, the first LT1054 inverts to about -5 V. A 2N2219 with its base grounded through 1k connects that rail to the second LT1054's GND pin, so the second part sits between 5 V and the -5 V rail. The second part makes about -12 V at its output and, with a diode-capacitor pump on CAP+, about +12 V; each rail gives 25 mA. The second part's oscillator, pulled up to its VREF by 20k, is driven through a Schottky from pin 4 of the first part.
notes: VIN = 5 V; VOUT ≈ 12 V and ≈ -12 V, IOUT = 25 mA each.

circuits.title: Strain gauge bridge signal conditioner
circuits.description: A 350 Ω bridge is excited from 5 V through 40 Ω at the top and through a 2N2222 to the LT1054's negative output at the bottom. Half of an LT1013 (A1) watches one bridge side and drives the LT1054's FB/SHDN through 200k, so the negative drive is servoed; the other half (A2) amplifies the bridge difference with a gain of about 125. A 2N2907, turned on by a TTL or CMOS low, supplies the LT1013 and the zero trim.

parts.note: dual op amp; A1 pins 1-3, A2 pins 5-7, supply pins 8 and 4
zero trim potentiometer, wiper to R5

notes: A = 125, giving 0 V to 3 V out for a full-scale bridge output of 24 mV.
The input is a TTL or CMOS level, low for on.
The zero trim is a 10k potentiometer between the switched supply and ground with its wiper to the 301k resistor.

circuits.title: 3.5V to 5V regulator
circuits.description: Makes a regulated 5 V from 3.5 V to 5.5 V at up to 50 mA. The LT1054 is supplied from the + output rail, which also drives its FB/SHDN pin and is fed from VIN through 20k and a 1N914; an LTC1044 inverter run from VIN supplies a negative point at the end of the upper R2. The 5 V output is taken between the + rail and a - rail tied to a diode-connected 2N2219 above the LT1054 output, with a 1N5817 from the LT1054 output to ground and a 1N914 from the - rail to ground.

parts.note: switched-capacitor voltage inverter, pin numbers as drawn
from the R1 junction to the LTC1044 output

notes: VIN = 3.5 V to 5.5 V; VOUT = 5 V; IOUT(MAX) = 50 mA.

circuits.title: Regulating 200mA, 12V to -5V converter
circuits.description: Two LT1054s in parallel on one output and one feedback divider (R1 39.2k from the first part's VREF, R2 200k to the output, 0.002 µF across R2) give -5 V at up to 200 mA from 12 V. Each flying capacitor has a 10 Ω, 1/2 W resistor in series to take dissipation out of the packages. The second part's OSC, pulled up to its VREF by 20k, is driven from the first part's CAP+ through an HP5082-2810 Schottky.
notes: VOUT = -5 V; IOUT = 0 mA to 200 mA.

circuits.title: Digitally programmable negative supply
circuits.description: An AD558 DAC run from 15 V sets the output: its output feeds FB/SHDN through 20k, a second 20k runs from FB/SHDN to the LT1054 output, and an LT1004-2.5 reference sits between the DAC output and its second analogue pin, which returns to ground through a resistor. The output is the negative of the programmed DAC voltage.
notes: VOUT = -VIN (programmed).
The DAC's eight data inputs are one bus; the second analogue pin joined to the LT1004 carries no number.

circuits.title: Positive doubler with regulation
circuits.description: A 5 V to 8 V, 50 mA doubler with its output regulated. CAP+ pumps a 10 µF capacitor charged from VIN through one 1N5817; a second 1N5817 passes the peak to the output. An LT1006 compares the divided output (5.5k over 2.5k, through 10k) with the LT1054's VREF, filtered by 0.1 µF, and drives FB/SHDN through 10k against a 50k pull-up to VIN; 0.03 µF in series with 10k compensates the loop.
notes: VIN = 5 V; VOUT = 8 V at 50 mA.

circuits.title: Negative doubler with regulator
circuits.description: A negative doubler (two 10 µF flying capacitors, two 1N4001 diodes) whose output is regulated through R1 20k from VREF and an adjustable 1M R2 from the output to FB/SHDN, with 0.002 µF across R2.
notes: VIN = 3.5 V to 15 V; VOUT(MAX) ≈ -2VIN + (VL + 2VDIODE), VL being the LT1054 voltage loss.

operation.text: A bipolar monolithic switched-capacitor converter with a built-in reference and error amplifier. It inverts its input with about 1.1 V lost at 100 mA over a 3.5 V to 15 V supply, and an external resistor divider turns it into a regulator that holds the output against input and load changes. An adaptive switch driver keeps efficiency up across the output current range. Quiescent current is about 2.5 mA; grounding FB/SHDN shuts it down to under 100 µA. The oscillator runs nominally at 25 kHz and can be retuned or synchronised through OSC. It is pin compatible with the LTC1044 and ICL7660 and can be paralleled.

In the basic building block a switch connects C1 first to V1, charging it to q1 = C1V1, then to V2, where its charge becomes q2 = C1V2. Repeated f times a second this moves a current f·C1(V1 – V2), so the network acts as a resistor REQUIV = 1/(fC1). The LT1054 switches the same way. At low frequency the 1/fC1 term dominates and losses rise; at high frequency the charge lost in each switching transition becomes a significant current and losses rise again. The oscillator sits in the band of least loss.

Below about 0.45 V on FB/SHDN the part shuts down. An unregulated circuit starts again as soon as the pull-down is released. In a regulating circuit the feedback divider can hold FB/SHDN low until COUT has fully discharged; where the part must restart sooner, a restart signal (a pulse over 100 µs or a logic high) is diode-coupled into FB/SHDN as in the basic regulator with shutdown and restart inputs, with R3/R4 giving 0.7 V to 1.1 V there, and the output comes up without overshoot.

operation.topic: Loads returned to a positive supply
operation.text: VOUT is the substrate. A load returned to V+ or another positive voltage (most op amps, whose supply current flows from V+ to V–) can pull VOUT above GND during start-up, forward-biasing the substrate diode so the part does not start. An NPN such as a 2N2222 or 2N2219, or sometimes an enhancement-mode N-channel MOSFET, placed between the load and VOUT prevents this; RX is sized so the transistor stays saturated.

OSC is the timing capacitor node (Ct ≈ 150 pF, ±7 µA, about 50% duty). An external capacitor from OSC to ground lowers the frequency; 5 pF to 20 pF from CAP+ to OSC couples charge into Ct at each transition and raises it. For synchronisation OSC gets a 20k pull-up to VREF and an open-collector gate or NPN pulls it at the clock rate; pulling OSC up to an external voltage is not recommended. A circuit that needs both synchronisation and regulation can take the top of the R1/R2 divider from an external reference and keep VREF for the OSC pull-up.

VREF is 2.5 V with a deliberately positive temperature coefficient that offsets drift in the internal divider and comparator, leaving a regulated output with a slight positive TC below 5 V and a slight negative TC above 5 V. Feedback loading should stay near 60 µA. A short to ground draws about 100 µA and does not disturb the regulator.

V+ charges CIN when CIN is across the supply and CIN then delivers charge to COUT. Supply current peaks near 2.2 × IOUT during charging and drops to about 0.2 × IOUT during transfer. The input bypass capacitor supplies part of the peaks; at least 2 µF, tantalum or another low-ESR type, is recommended, and more where the supply arrives through long leads or the pulse current could couple into other circuits.

The error amplifier controls the drive to the PNP switch and so the voltage on CIN, which sets the output. R1 should be 20k or more because the reference can supply only about 100 µA; R2 should be 100k to 300k. CIN/COUT of 1/10 is recommended, and C1 = 0.002 µF across R2 gives good regulation at light load for every output voltage. In the plain inverter, |VOUT| measured from GND has to stay under the supply less the switch voltage loss; a negative doubler reaches higher outputs at lower current.

The LT1054CS8 uses a new die to fit the package. It meets every specification, but in regulating circuits its CIN and COUT nominal values must be about equal for correct operation at high junction temperature, unlike the earlier part; normal capacitor tolerances are acceptable and transient response is slightly worse. Unregulated circuits use equal CIN and COUT on all packages.

Unregulated circuits use equal nominal CIN and COUT; exact values are not critical but the capacitors must be low-ESR, such as solid tantalum. ESR in CIN counts four times, since switch current is about twice the output current and flows on charge and discharge: 1 Ω of ESR acts like 4 Ω more output impedance. ESR in COUT, which carries about the output current, adds a step to the ripple at each transition that worsens load regulation. A small tantalum in parallel with a large aluminium electrolytic gives low ESR at modest cost; surface-mount chip tantalums rated 10 V to 20 V offer ESR near 0.1 Ω.

Dissipation comes from voltage drop in the switches and from drive current; in regulating circuits it equals that of a linear regulator. With a large input-output difference, output current must be limited or a resistor put in series with CIN to drop part of the input outside the package. In the 12 V to -5 V, 100 mA example 940 mW at 130°C/W raises the junction 122°C, beyond the limit at 25°C ambient; an 11 Ω RX removes 490 mW, leaving 450 mW and a 58°C rise. Specifications are guaranteed only to 100°C junction (functionality to 125°C), which in this example means 42°C ambient at most. The θJA values are worst case in still air without heat sinking; clip-on heat sinks, airflow and wide copper traces from the leads lower them, especially for plastic packages.
The typical application circuits were checked with the standard LT1054 die, not the S8.
